routing.reason: Small, well-specified validation and error-handling fix in a ~340-line app (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js, tests), with testable acceptance criteria already listed.
rulings: Ruling: workflow default, not hotfix — a 500 on invalid input is a bug but not an urgent outage, and the plan gate is cheap on an S change — cost if wrong: one extra gate
Ruling: skip frame (po) — the ticket already lists 7 testable acceptance criteria, framing them again only repeats them — cost if wrong: a missed edge case surfaces at code review
Ruling: skip prd, architecture, ux, seo — not a vague epic, no cross-cutting decision, only an error line on the existing page, no public page change — cost if wrong: minor rework
Ruling: security effort medium — input validation and error-message leakage (A10:2025) are in scope, but no auth, payments or personal data — cost if wrong: a missed leak of an internal message
Ruling: budget $1.50 — S change covering one implement task, review rounds and the security review — cost if wrong: run stops before its reviews and needs a top-up

criteria.why: parseTitle rejects missing, empty, blank and non-string titles with 400 'title is required' before insert; tested.
PATCH uses Object.hasOwn(body,'title') and parseTitle, so null/empty titles are rejected; tested.
parseTitle enforces a 200-character limit after trimming with the exact message and returns the trimmed title; tested.
readJson converts parse failures (and non-object JSON) to ValidationError 'invalid JSON body', which is answered with 400.
The catch handler logs with console.error and sends the generic 'internal error' message with 500.
The submit handler wraps the call in try/catch and calls show(err), assuming api() throws with the API error message.
New tests cover POST, PATCH, length, trimming, invalid JSON and the 500 path. The page change is untested.

findings.what: createTask calls parseTitle again, and app.ts already called it, so POST validates twice. updateTask does the same for PATCH. The redundancy is harmless but muddles where validation belongs.
PATCH validates the title before the task lookup, so a nonexistent id with a bad title returns 400, not 404. This is deliberate and tested, but it is not in the ticket.
Rejecting valid non-object JSON ('null', '[]', '5') as 'invalid JSON body' goes slightly beyond the ticket, though it is reasonable and documented. The res.headersSent guard is also extra.
The front-end error display (criterion 6) has no test. The 500 test depends on dropping the table from a second connection, which is a bit fragile.
PATCH still passes body.done unvalidated, which is outside this ticket. The readJson loop also has no body size limit, which is pre-existing.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion. It uses one shared parseTitle validator, a ValidationError class mapped to 400, a generic logged 500, and a try/catch on the page. Tests are thorough and the README is updated; the weak spots are validation running twice, no test for the page change, and a few small additions beyond the ticket.
